description: Opera Canada is a quarterly about opera in Canada and Canadians working in opera abroad, with artist profiles, company features, performance reviews, a masterclass column and an annual ranking of Canadian companies. The fall number doubles as the programme for the magazine's own awards. It is for opera goers, singers and people working in the performing arts.

OSMOS Magazine is a New York art magazine about photography and how images are used, mixing critical essays, artist conversations, portfolios and reportage in recurring thematic sections. Issues run to around 100 pages and connect to the publisher's exhibition programme. It is for readers of contemporary art criticism and photography.

PLS is the French language magazine of the Palais de Tokyo, issued with each new exhibition season. Every number takes one theme, such as territory or the body, and gathers essays and visual contributions from the artists and researchers connected to the current shows. It is for readers following French contemporary art and the Palais de Tokyo programme.

Permanent Style is a print menswear magazine grown out of the website of the same name, focused on tailoring, craft and the makers behind classic men's clothing. Each issue carries long interviews and reportage, often built around a city or region, with recent numbers on Scotland and Los Angeles. It is for readers interested in bespoke clothing, shoemaking and well made menswear.

Port is a large format London biannual covering culture and style through long interviews with actors, writers, designers and architects, photo led fashion stories and essays on art, design, food and literature. Issues run to around 300 pages with several covers. It is for readers who want a glossy but text heavy general culture magazine with a menswear slant.

Prairie Fire is a Winnipeg literary quarterly publishing new fiction, poetry and creative non fiction, with themed issues and annual writing contests. It is printed as a perfect bound journal and draws on writers from the Prairies and across Canada. It is for readers of literary journals and emerging Canadian writing.

Profane is a French biannual art review devoted to amateurs, self taught makers and collectors working outside the official art world. Each issue mixes portraits, interviews and photo stories of people who make or collect for love rather than career, set in experimental graphic design. It is for readers of art, craft and outsider culture, in French.

Pulp Literature is a Canadian quarterly digest of genre fiction, poetry and comics, leaning towards science fiction, fantasy and mystery alongside literary work. Issues run serialised novellas, contest winners and feature authors in a pocketable, inexpensive format. It is for readers who like story driven fiction they can carry around.

Ralph is a glossy London quarterly about pop culture and entertainment, with long interviews with comedians, musicians, television people and animators alongside photo stories and humour pieces. It is deliberately playful and broad rather than niche. It is for readers who want a fun, mainstream leaning entertainment magazine in print.

Real Review is a tall, narrow pocket format magazine from London that treats architecture, politics, technology and everyday objects as subjects for short critical reviews gathered around a theme or mood per issue. The latest number is built around pretending and performance in public life. It suits readers of architecture criticism and cultural theory who like dense, designed print.

Richardson is a large format occasional magazine from New York that mixes sexually explicit photography with essays, fiction and interviews from artists and writers, each issue built around a theme. The latest, A12, is the California issue with a cover by Harley Weir. It sits between an art book and a fashion magazine and is for adult readers interested in subcultural photography and provocative writing.

Riddle Fence is a journal of arts and culture from Newfoundland and Labrador that prints poetry, short fiction, creative non fiction, features and reviews alongside contemporary visual art, with a strong regional base and contributors from across Canada and beyond. Issues carry contest winners and themed features three times a year. It is for readers of Canadian literary magazines and the Atlantic arts scene.

Sandweegies is a Glasgow food magazine that uses one kind of sandwich per issue as a way into the city's cafes, bakeries, chefs and eating habits, with photography led features and strong graphic design. Issues so far cover the chicken sandwich, the breakfast roll and the fish sandwich. It is for people interested in Scottish food culture and city life rather than recipes.

Sex Magazine is a print only interview magazine that profiles musicians, artists, writers, filmmakers and internet personalities on the edge of pop culture through long conversations and portrait photography, and despite the name is not about sex. The latest issue leads with John Maus and includes Dennis Cooper and Shlohmo. It is for readers who follow underground music, art and online subcultures.

SHADOWPLAY is a thick art and beauty publication from the makers of Behind the Blinds, built from photographic portfolios, interviews and essays that treat beauty as a subject across fashion, art, music and film. Each issue is released with a dozen or more alternate covers featuring artists, musicians and models. It is for collectors of photography led fashion and art magazines.

Sonshine is a quarterly parenting magazine about raising boys without gender stereotypes, with each issue built around a theme such as masculinity, clothes, bodies or books. It mixes advice articles, interviews, recipes, crafts, book reviews and puzzle pages for children. It is for parents and carers of boys who want a feminist angle on boyhood.

Spacing is a landscape format quarterly about Toronto's public realm, from transit, streets, housing and parks to urban design, civic politics and city history, with a themed feature section each issue. The latest number profiles the people and groups shaping the 2026 municipal election. It is for readers interested in how Canadian cities work and who want to get involved.

Stranger's Guide is a book like print series from Austin in which each issue is devoted to one place or theme and gathers long form reporting, essays, fiction and photography, mostly by writers from that place. The latest edition is a photography led issue on work and labour around the world. It is for readers who want literary, place based journalism rather than travel tips.

description: STUDY is an English language publication from Paris in which each volume examines one person, place or idea through portfolios, conversations, essays, fashion editorials and archival documents, in a format designed to be kept rather than read once. Volume 16 revisits 1920s European modernist interiors through the archive of photographer Thérèse Bonney. It is for readers of fashion, art and design publishing who collect photography books.

description: subTerrain is a Vancouver literary magazine mixing short fiction, poetry, essays and commentary with book reviews and columns on chapbooks and small press publishing. Each issue carries a featured visual artist on the cover and inside, and some numbers are built around a theme such as dreams or trash. It is for readers of contemporary Canadian and international writing with a stake in the small press scene.
